the City of Hamilton, Ontario, the first jurisdiction to open. Section 9 records the owner's 2026-10-18 decisions. Thresholds, gate rules and size budgets in sections 2, 3 and 6 are ACCEPTED.
One staged beta gate, for now.
G5 ("reconciled") and G6 ("publish") are merged into one gate with two stages (the owner, 2026-10-18). They may split again after beta.
Spine, joins, labelling, screening and reproducibility checks pass for the jurisdiction (sections 2 to 5).
Pre-publish checks pass on the actual build output, the deploy path works, and the owner signs off (sections 6 to 8).
Each jurisdiction opens on its own checklist. Hamilton does not wait for Niagara, Western New York or any other area. A later jurisdiction reuses this document as a template.
"Reconciled" means observed and labelled, not made clean.

Every known conflict, gap, sliver and contradiction is detected, classified, counted and labelled. Nothing is extinguished from view to make the data look tidier. Some classes are flagged as must-solve before publishing (section 4).

The checks, metrics, run records and labels are universal back-end work (Industrial Atlas). How they appear on heavymap.com is front-end work (HeavyMap.com project) and is out of scope here, apart from naming what must be surfaced.
Repo split (plan recorded in PR #80; execution separately assigned).

Keep everything in this repo during concurrent work. Do not create the new repository, move paths or rename identifiers without a separate bounded assignment. Frontend repair and backend validation proceed independently of migration timing.

Each check runs on every build. Each one writes a value into the run record (section 3). The same definitions apply to every jurisdiction. Only the thresholds may differ, and any difference must be written down.

— Metric: One-to-one rate · How it is computed: Reciprocal representative-point matches between City parcels and the attribute fabric, after the offset is applied. Divided by attribute-fabric parcels in the overlap set. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): 90,102 pairs, 99.77% · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): warn below 99.5%, fail below 99.0%

— Metric: One-to-one quality · How it is computed: Overlap ratio (IoU) of S1 pairs: p10, p50, p90, and the count with IoU ≥ 0.9. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): p10 0.999, p50 1.000, p90 1.000; 89,837 at ≥ 0.9 · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): fail if p10 < 0.95

— Metric: One-to-many and many-to-one · How it is computed: Count of City parcels linked to more than one identifier, and identifiers linked to more than one City parcel. Placeholders are excluded (see S5). · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): Recorded in registry

— Metric: Unmatched · How it is computed: City parcels in the overlap set with no identifier, and attribute-fabric parcels with no City parcel. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): Recount after the batched re-run · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): ≤ 0.5% each, every one labelled

— Metric: Not in coverage · How it is computed: City parcels outside the attribute fabric's footprint. Graded

, tied to the dataset that defines the coverage. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): 74,276 of 166,745 (GAP-0010) · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): Labelled, no fail level (coverage is a fact about the source)

— Metric: Offset applied · How it is computed: The measured translation between fabrics (median dx, dy), its spread (IQR) and the sample size. The build fails if the offset in use differs from the offset measured on this pull by more than a tolerance. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): dx +0.297 m, dy −0.939 m, IQR < 3 mm (Q-004, NA-276) · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): tolerance 0.05 m; IQR ≤ 0.01 m
— Metric: ID stability across runs · How it is computed: Between this run and the previous registry: kept,

, newly minted, retired. On an unchanged input, every ID must be kept. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): Synthetic test passes; first real repeat pending · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): Unchanged input: 100% kept (hard). Changed input: reported

— Metric: Overlay link coverage · How it is computed: For each overlay layer (zoning, OP designations, conservation and so on): the share of City parcels with at least one link, plus layers present with zero links. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): 644,398 links over all parcels · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): every layer has ≥ 1 link or a gap entry explaining why not

— Metric: Sliver counts · How it is computed: Links whose area share falls under the sliver rule, per layer. Flagged, never dropped. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): 150,610 of 644,398 flagged · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): Reported, no fail level (flag, never extinguish)

— Metric: Address and footprint linkage · How it is computed: Addresses inside exactly one parcel, more than one, or none. Footprints the same way. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): 273,955 addresses, 214,287 buildings registered · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): reported; "none" cases labelled

— Metric: Row-count drift · How it is computed: Rows per source layer against the previous pull. · Hamilton today (2026-10-17 run): First baseline 2026-10-17 · Threshold (ACCEPTED 2026-10-18): warn at > 2% change, explain at > 5%
The 644,398 figure is parcel-to-overlay-feature links (about 3.9 per City parcel on 166,745 parcels, including 150,610 slivers), not a parcel count. PI-0063.

Row-count drift is how we tell a publisher change from a broken pull (truncated download, paging failure, swapped layer). A warn or explain is not automatically a fail; the explanation must say which of those it is.
A check that cannot be computed writes a blank with a reason, never a zero (HARD-RULES 8).

4. Labelling: every known conflict observed and labelled
One taxonomy, 1:1 with the tracking sheets.
Each class of issue has one label code. Each code maps to exactly one class in the tracking CSVs:
A new class gets a code, a plain-language definition and a sheet home before it is used. A label with no sheet home fails the build.
They stay their own set, separate from claim-refusal reasons, with a documented mapping between the two (decided 2026-10-17).
